supporting_evidence.quote: ROI benefited from increased operating income due to improved business performance, which was partially offset by the incremental non-cash share-based compensation charge at PhonePe as well as certain legal matters and other business restructuring charges.

Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales increased 64 and 35 basis points for the three and six months ended July 31, 2025, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year, which reflect charges of $0.4 billion related to certain legal matters.

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Walmart's consolidated operating income in fiscal 2026 was reduced by legal and restructuring charges. This is a qualitative/interpretive claim about what factors affected operating income, without making specific numeric assertions.

Evidence E1 directly supports this claim by stating that operating income was "partially offset by the incremental non-cash share-based compensation charge at PhonePe as well as certain legal matters and other business restructuring charges" in fiscal 2026 (the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026).

Evidence E5 provides additional support by documenting charges of $0.4 billion related to certain legal matters during the six months ended July 31, 2025 (which falls within fiscal 2026), and notes these charges increased operating expenses as a percentage of net sales.

Both pieces of evidence confirm that legal matters and restructuring charges reduced operating income in fiscal 2026, fully supporting the claim.
